description: loop() and while() statements and their iteration cap. The two-argument while(cond, body) form is a dialect extension shared with projectM and Butterchurn; ns-eel2 registers while with one argument, so the same programs read while(exec2(body, cond)) there.

cases.name: loop(n, body) runs the body n times
a loop count truncates toward zero
a negative loop count runs the body zero times
a loop body may hold several statements separated by semicolons
while(cond, body) repeats until the condition is zero
a while() condition uses the close-factor threshold, like every other boolean context
cases.note: Pinned by the ns-eel2 source: nseel_asm_repeatwhile (asm-nseel-x86-gcc.c) evaluates the condition, takes fabs, and fcomp's it against [g_closefact] (NSEEL_CLOSEFACTOR = 0.00001, ns-eel-int.h:56), so the body runs only while |cond| is at least the close factor. Modern EEL2 boolifies the same way (nseel_asm_fptobool / EEL_BC_FPTOBOOL: fabs(v) >= NSEEL_CLOSEFACTOR). A condition of 1e-6 is therefore false before the first iteration: the body never runs, x stays 0 and n keeps its 1e-6. The id names the question this case once asked (it was provisional, pinning exact zero) and is kept stable; the value was corrected on 2026-10-28.
